corrections: Replaced the generic airframe with individually measured Cessna 172S cowling, one-piece windscreen, door/rear windows and aft Omni-Vision glazing, hollow cabin, strut-supported high wing and swept tail. Corrected reversed right window contours during review.

Matched 36 ft 1 in span, 27 ft 2 in length, 65 inch wheelbase and 76 inch propeller. Moved the stabilizer forward after the planform overlay; modeled separate elevators, rudder, flap and aileron pivots, wheel fairings, skin joints and selected rivet rows.

Rebuilt the NAV III/GFC700 cockpit around dimensioned 10.4 inch GDU displays and GMA1347 audio panel, three standby instruments, physical yokes, push-pull controls, breaker banks, trim/fuel pedestal, pedals and four seats. Corrected glare-shield depth and cross-section after seated and exterior inspection.

Added reusable instrument geometry wired through public instrument helpers and the expression graph. Live PFD attitude, speed tape/digits, geometric altitude including negative values, true heading, vertical-speed pointer and 10-RPM readout use actual scene state. Standby speed has a photo-measured nonlinear scale; three altimeter pointers use distinct gear ratios. No fuel, oil or map readings are invented.

Added imported-model regressions for readings, missing-data blanking, negative altitude, bank/pitch signs and both side-window sightlines. Numeric visual inspection exposed and corrected meter-to-foot truncation at integer boundaries.
reviewNotes.visual: Individually inspected side, top, front and panel overlays; four turntable angles, three-quarter, seated operator, cabin and cabin-wide renders. Repeated affected captures after window, stabilizer, coaming and instrument corrections. Inspected zero, 120-knot/3500-ft/2400-RPM cruise, 163-knot/12500-ft/2700-RPM and missing-sensor/-100-ft instrument cases; bank and pitch varied independently.
limitations: The manufacturer three-view is schematic: the front propeller disk is drawn nearly touching the ground despite 11.25-inch specified clearance, and its wing height disagrees with the side view. The side drawing is a normal static attitude, below the stated maximum overall height. Uniform overlays retain those residuals; independent dimensions and exterior photos take precedence.

Panel placement uses a dimensioned Garmin bezel to scale the Cessna handbook photograph. Perspective, callout lines and unknown panel depth limit exact comparisons. The separate Creative Commons cockpit photograph has an older autopilot fit and displays in reversionary mode; it informs details, not the selected avionics configuration.

Flight dynamics remain assisted tuning. Speed is currently true airspeed, explicitly labeled TAS; altitude is geometric world elevation, labeled GEO FT; heading is true rather than magnetic. Pressure instruments, magnetic variation, electrical/vacuum failure models, full G1000 menus, radios, navigation, fuel and oil systems are not implemented. Gauges show available data with approximate response constants, not certified instrument dynamics.

Standby dial angles are estimated from a perspective photograph. Colored ranges follow the Cessna handbook but are not operational IAS limits when the current display is driven by TAS. Cross-sections, upholstery, fastener patterns and wheel fairings remain polygonal approximations; rivet rows are not a manufacturing rivet map.
Photographs and drawings remain local study inputs; no source image pixels or photorealistic textures are distributed.

units.heading: true north clockwise radians derived from simulation yaw
units.rpm: engine-1 normalized propeller speed multiplied by declared 2700 RPM

controlReview.checks: Imported GLB control-point movement tested at positive and negative commands; all 20 aircraft pass. Cockpit pairs and all ten airplane exterior pairs visually inspected. Roll, pitch, rudder and declared pedal directions corrected; ailerons and full flap deployment corrected.
limitations: Checks cover existing bindings; Cherokee and Caravan pedal geometry is static.
Full control travel and flight response remain approximations unless independently dimensioned in the model reference notes.
This audit verifies movement; it does not upgrade legacy helicopter avionics or remove previously documented geometry limitations.
